page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data positions the ecs.g6.2xlarge primarily in the average performance tier for multi-core and memory operations. Multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls within the middle 50% of tested instances. Memory bandwidth tests, including uncached large-block reads at 48.91 GB/sec and writes at 37.78 GB/sec, also demonstrate mid-tier capabilities. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core, single-threaded gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression benchmarks scoring in the bottom 25%.

Given its balanced hardware profile and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.g6.2xlarge offers a stable resource density for general-purpose workloads. It is suited for applications requiring moderate multi-threaded processing and balanced memory allocation, such as medium-scale database operations, text processing, and software compilation. The lack of local storage and lower single-threaded performance represent tradeoffs that make it less suitable for high-throughput static web serving or intensive single-core compute tasks.
